_doc: Engineered freeway interchanges, generated parametrically by tools/lib/interchange.py. kind 'diamond': 4 one-way ramps (exit before / entrance after the crossroad, per direction), crossroad carried OVER the freeway. ramp_offset_px = freeway distance from crossing to the ramp gore; terminal_offset_px = distance along the crossroad from the freeway centreline to each ramp terminal. 1 px = 2.5 m.

interchanges.name: SR 60 / US 76 Interchange
interchanges.note: Compressed diamond: the south-side ramps are short because SR 60 crosses the Tanner immediately south; the NB exit crosses the creek inlet on a short structure.

interchanges.name: SR 60 / Riverfront Pkwy grade separation
interchanges.note: Was a half diamond. Vertical design makes it infeasible: SR 60 descends from the US 76 diamond to its Tanner River bridge at the 6% freeway limit and is 10-17 m above the river bank here, so ramps down to Riverfront Pkwy would need ~12% grades. SR 60 now crosses over Riverfront Pkwy on its river-bridge approach viaduct (upper=freeway); Tannersville traffic uses the SR 60/US 76 diamond.

interchanges.name: SR 9 wye (Northwest / Spur split)
interchanges.note: Directional split of SR 9 (right-hand traffic). The through route is Downtown Connector <-> Spur; the Northwest branch separates into two one-way roadways: westbound traffic leaves the northbound trunk on the right, flies over the whole trunk (clearance >= 4.9 m below the deck) and comes down beside the southbound lanes to SR 9 NW's westbound carriageway; eastbound SR 9 NW traffic runs outside it and becomes an added lane on the southbound trunk. Offsets: [px along the trunk from the split, px off its centreline (positive = north-east)]; flyover_ext_px: straight run past the split [px, offset] before joining the branch.
